knowledge_base.quantum_concern: Low (Grover's algorithm halves effective bits; 256-bit retains 128-bit quantum security)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Maintain AES-256; AES-128 is acceptable but consider transitioning to AES-256 for long-term security.
knowledge_base.description: Galois/Counter Mode provides authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD). Highly secure and efficient.

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Migrate to AEAD mode like AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 to prevent padding oracle vulnerabilities.
knowledge_base.description: Cipher Block Chaining mode. Lacks built-in authentication; susceptible to padding oracle attacks if not combined with HMAC (Encrypt-then-MAC).

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Replace immediately with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.
knowledge_base.description: Electronic Codebook mode does not hide data patterns. Identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: High (Small 64-bit block size susceptible to Sweet32 attack)
knowledge_base.description: Triple DES uses a 64-bit block size vulnerable to collision attacks (Sweet32). Disallowed by NIST after 2023.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: Critical (Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm and feasible classical factorization)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Upgrade to RSA-3072/4096 or ECDSA (P-256) classically; evaluate NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) for PQC roadmap.
knowledge_base.description: 1024-bit RSA provides less than 80 bits of security and can be factored with moderate distributed computing power.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: High (Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on CRQC)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Plan migration to hybrid post-quantum schemes (e.g. ML-KEM / ML-DSA) or transition to 3072-bit for interim classical protection.
knowledge_base.description: 2048-bit RSA provides 112 bits of classical security. Adequate for current commercial use through 2030, but quantum-vulnerable.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: High (Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on CRQC)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Adopt hybrid key establishment with ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for long-term quantum resistance.
knowledge_base.description: 3072-bit RSA provides 128-bit security margin, compliant with NIST standards beyond 2030 for classical threats.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: Critical (Shor's algorithm solves ECDLP efficiently with fewer qubits than RSA)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Prepare transition to ML-KEM (Kyber) for KEM and ML-DSA (Dilithium) or SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+) for signatures.
knowledge_base.description: Elliptic Curve Cryptography providing 128-bit classical security with 256-bit keys. Excellent performance but vulnerable to quantum attacks.

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Deploy hybrid key exchange: X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (as in TLS 1.3 draft/X25519Kyber768Draft00).
knowledge_base.description: Modern, constant-time Montgomery curve key exchange. Highly resistant to side-channel attacks classically.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: High (Collisions practically generated classically; SHAttered / SHA-1 Chosen-Prefix)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Replace with SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA3-256 immediately.
knowledge_base.description: Collision resistance completely broken. Disallowed by NIST and major certificate authorities.

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Replace with SHA-256 or SHA3-256 for integrity; PBKDF2/Argon2id for passwords.
knowledge_base.description: Trivially vulnerable to collision and preimage attacks. Never use for digital signatures or security controls.

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: Low (Grover's algorithm reduces collision to 128-bit quantum security, which remains unbreakable)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Retain SHA-256 or adopt SHA-384/SHA-512 for higher quantum assurance.
knowledge_base.description: Standard secure hash algorithm providing 128-bit collision resistance and 256-bit preimage resistance.

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Upgrade to TLS 1.3 and disable TLS 1.0/1.1 completely across server configurations.
knowledge_base.description: Obsolete protocol vulnerable to BEAST, POODLE, and weak cipher negotiations. Deprecated by RFC 8996.
Deprecated by RFC 8996 due to lack of modern cipher suites and weak cryptographic hash dependencies.

knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Restrict to ECDHE + AES-GCM cipher suites and plan upgrade to TLS 1.3.
knowledge_base.description: Standard protocol when configured with secure AEAD cipher suites and PFS (Perfect Forward Secrecy).

knowledge_base.quantum_concern: Low to Medium (Supports hybrid PQC key exchange extensions)
knowledge_base.pqc_recommendation: Enable hybrid post-quantum key exchange (e.g. X25519+Kyber768 / X25519MLKEM768).
knowledge_base.description: State of the art transport protocol with mandatory forward secrecy, removed legacy ciphers, and 1-RTT handshake.
